Published online:
3 September 2026

Geographic focus:
Germany (Europe)

Temporal focus:
T1. Historical report [YES] — references Q2 2026 GDP growth of 0.3%
T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES] — export momentum expected to weaken later in 2026
T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES] — GDP forecasts through 2027–2028; structural headwinds flagged

Synopsis:
RWI sharply upgrades Germany's GDP growth forecast to 1.3% for 2026 (from 0.8%) and 1.1% for 2027 (from 0.8%), slowing to 0.5% in 2028. The Q2 2026 recovery was export-driven and partly temporary. Structural drags persist: high energy prices, weak competitiveness, bureaucratic burden, subdued private consumption, and labour-market uncertainty. The Iran conflict adds energy price pressure; U.S. tariffs create trade uncertainty.
